_about: What the Goals store opens with: only Rafael Duarte's armed critical stock watch and the two saved plans. Executed and Submissions start empty.

g-rule-stock-cover.title: No critical spare or chemical below safety stock: check every nightly load
g-rule-stock-cover.prompt: Keep every critical spare and treatment chemical above safety stock across all our sites. Check each nightly load of stock, open orders and work order reservations; when something is going to fall short before it can be replenished, size it, look at what the rest of the group holds, and work out what can still be done before I ask.

reads.res: Look across the group before an emergency purchase · the holder stays at or above its own safety stock · expedites up to $25k are approved by Rafael
Class A items · chemical cover 14 days water, 10 hazardous waste, 7 energy · outage materials ready 14 days ahead
2,782 critical positions at 36 sites · open lines with promised dates · reservations of released work orders
Stock, orders and reservations load nightly at 02:00. Next: tonight, Wednesday 28 October
"Treatment chemicals award" reads the same ferric cover; I read it whenever this fires

reads.tool: search for a storeroom distribution list
reads.res: No storeroom list is connected; I need to know who to tell
Critical positions below safety stock are reviewed daily · Ravensworth Kiln 2 outage from 9 November · Corrigan at 60% on ferric

questions.title: What should make it fire?
questions.text: Positions dip below safety stock every week and most have an order landing in time. The rule can fire only when something will run short before it can be replenished, or on every position below safety stock.

tiles.t: When a position will run short before its next receipt
Also when an outage reservation is not covered 14 days ahead
tiles.s: What the standard asks for outages

questions.title: Who is told when it fires?
questions.text: No storeroom list is connected. The note goes out without waiting for you, so pick who should see it.

tiles.t: Me, the buyers and the site leads
tiles.s: Everyone who can release or move stock

nodes.title: Confirm what the load flagged, and size it
nodes.purpose: Which positions will run short before they can be replenished, and by how much.
nodes.how: Every critical position against its safety stock, its reservations and its next confirmed receipt: on hand, what is needed by when, the shortfall. Limited to the positions in the load that fired the rule.
nodes.check: Every flagged position recomputes from on hand, safety stock, reservations and promised dates.

nodes.title: Why it happened, and whether anyone is on it
nodes.purpose: Is this new, and is someone already handling it.
nodes.how: Supplier date changes, released reservations, the Corrigan allocation, and what the buyers, the outage manager and the plants have said.
draws: Outlook: outage, buyers, plants (R1, R2, F2)
nodes.check: Every cause is dated and sourced.

nodes.title: Look across the group: stock, expedites, substitutes
nodes.purpose: What the rest of the group holds, and what the suppliers can still do.
nodes.how: For each position: other sites holding the same material above their own safety stock, the freight to move it, expedites the suppliers have offered, and approved substitutes.
nodes.check: No holder is taken below its own safety stock.

nodes.title: What can still be done, including nothing
nodes.purpose: Each course of action with what it costs and what it protects, checked against open goals.
nodes.how: Each option with its cost, the positions it covers, the days of outage it protects, who has to agree, and an honest statement where nothing can be done in time; read the open goals on this role.
nodes.check: Every option states what it costs and what it covers.

nodes.title: Build the deliverables, act and tell you
nodes.purpose: Build what was agreed at set-up, take the actions that run by themselves, hold the others for your OK, and tell the people you chose.
nodes.how: The positions, why they are short, what the group holds, the options and the moves; on the stock exception note template.
nodes.check: Every figure in the note links back to its step.

chat.text: Keep every critical spare and treatment chemical above safety stock across all our sites. Check each nightly load of stock, open orders and work order reservations; when something is going to fall short before it can be replenished, size it, look at what the rest of the group holds, and work out what can still be done before I ask.
Watch armed · v1 · 21 Oct, 16:40 · Rafael Duarte

Armed. I check every critical position at the nightly load (02:00) against its safety stock, its reservations and its next confirmed receipt. Nothing runs until a position will run short before it can be replenished, or an outage reservation is not covered 14 days ahead.

The plan on the right is what runs when it fires: five steps, no checkpoint. Then I choose the top option, build the stock exception note and the transfer list, do the actions agreed at set-up and tell you, the buyers and the site leads. Anything that goes to a supplier or costs money waits for your OK.
27 Oct · 02:00 load checked · 20 below safety stock, none short before its next receipt · next: tonight, 02:00

saved.name: Chemicals award: spend, cover, bids, continuity
saved.prompt: Helena needs the treatment chemicals award for the Procurement Committee on Thursday 12 November, with the paper by 5 November. Work out what we buy across Water, Hazardous Waste and Energy and what it costs today, compare the bids in SE-2026-031 on landed cost, show how many days of cover each plant holds under the Corrigan force majeure, and draft the award paper, the award schedule in the 2024 structure and a few slides for the committee. Attached: the bid comparison export and the 2024 award schedule.
steps: State what the group buys and what it costs today
Check supply today: cover at each plant and the Corrigan allocation
Compare the bids on landed cost
Check qualification and continuity of each awarded bidder
